title: AI-Based Real-Time Elephant Monitoring and Human Elephant Conflict Mitigation System
summary: Mbeya University of Science and Technology plans a machine-learning module that would predict elephant conflicts from movement logs; its current prototype uses GPS and fixed geofences.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: The existing prototype tracks GPS positions, applies fixed geofences, and sends alerts through conventional electronics. A future machine-learning module would use movement logs and contextual data to predict elephant behavior and conflicts, with the aim of protecting people, crops, and wildlife. The project is led by Mbeya University of Science and Technology in Tanzania, with the Tanzania Wildlife Research Institute and the Tanzania National Parks Authority named as partners. By October 2026 no report of a field deployment or of the planned machine-learning module had appeared.
purpose: Predict elephant conflicts to support earlier protective action.
system: AI-Based Real-Time Elephant Monitoring and Human Elephant Conflict Mitigation System
developer: Mbeya University of Science and Technology
location: Tanzanian elephant corridors near farms and villages (planned)

data.answer:
MUST proposes learning from elephant movement logs to predict conflicts; its existing GPS and fixed-geofence prototype is not counted as an AI benefit.

The stated current logic is rule-based, with machine learning reserved for later behavioral prediction. No field conflict, crop-loss, or injury reduction is measured. GPS tracking and alerts alone therefore do not establish a realized AI benefit or safe, effective deterrence.

Future ML would infer behavior and conflict risk from logged movements and contextual data, beyond fixed proximity thresholds.
